newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Louis Dreyfus Citrus to invest in Brazil oranges.
newsitem.headline: Louis Dreyfus Citrus to invest in Brazil oranges.

text.p: Louis Dreyfus Citrus is to invest a total of $32 million over the next four to five years in Brazilian orange production, said the company's executive director.
The company plans to plant one million trees at three farms it has purchased in Sao Paulo state.
It will also look for suitable properties to plant a further one million trees, with an eventual production goal of around seven million 40.8-kg boxes, said Kenneth Geld.

The company, which currently has no production in Brazil, processes around 42 million boxes a year in its two plants in Sao Paulo state and a third plant it leases in Sergipe, and is seeking to produce up to 15 percent of its processing needs.
"I think 12 to 15 percent would be more or less the range," Geld said.

Louis Dreyfus Citrus, which is the world's third largest producer of orange juice, also is investing $16 million in expanding capacity and storage space and modernising the blending unit of its Winter Garden processing plant in Florida.
The investment should mean annual capacity at the plant, bought last September for $16 million, will increase to 14 million boxes from a current level of nine million boxes.
"This will be ready for the 1997/98 Florida season," Geld said.
Of the $16 million in new investments, the company has spent $5 million in buying equipment in Brazil for the U.S. plant.
"The price was very competitive and the technology is very similar to what is available in the U.S.," Geld said.
